newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's former top cop faces probe on payments.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's former top cop faces probe on payments.

text.p: Mexico's former Attorney General Antonio Lozano on Thursday was ordered to explain allegedly unauthorised payments of almost $1 million while in office, a demand he said was politically motivated.

Lozano, who from 1994-1996 was the only opposition politician in the cabinet of President Ernesto Zedillo, will be asked to explain to the Comptroller General's Office on March 20 why an unauthorised $875,000 was paid under his watch to witnesses in an investigation into a top political killing.

A statement by the Comptroller General's Office also said he would be asked to explain $55,000 of public money he spent or borrowed for personal use, as well the hiring of family and friends for government jobs.

Lozano was fired in December 1996 as a result of bungled investigations into the assassinations of two top ruling party officials in 1994. Following his dismissal, a scandal blew up over the payment of rewards to witnesses who allegedly fabricated evidence.

On Thursday, Lozano admitted making some of the payments, though he said no wrongdoing was involved. He accused the authorities of "mixing truths and half truths" to smear him and his National Action Party (PAN), Mexico's main opposition force that has campaigned against corruption.
He said the charges were leveled with an eye on mid-term Congressional elections in July, and he accused the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of being behind them.
"There is a political backdrop to all this...fear over the electoral process underway," he said.
The PRI, which has held power in Mexico since 1929, is expected to face difficulties in the elections. Its leader, Humberto Roque, on Thursday sought to capitalise on the investigation.
"The morality that (the PAN) claims it has is not what it puts into practice," Lozano told reporters.
